newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX oil futures on defense, await stoc.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX oil futures on defense, await stoc.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Crude and products are seen staying on the defensive with plenty of buying seen around but little above support levels.
* The oil complex will be looking ahead to this week's inventory data to determine whether demand in unleaded gasoline will lend enough support to lead the complex in the short term.
NYMEX crude and products futures are seen staying on the defensive with plenty of buying seen around but little above support levels, analysts and brokers said.
They said the oil complex will be looking ahead to this week's inventory data to determine whether demand in unleaded gasoline will lend enough support to lead the complex in the short term.
With peak demand season for unleaded gasoline at hand from last weekend's unofficial beginning of summer in the U.S., crude oil should be taking a back seat but demand for gasoline remains slow.

"We are now supposedly in the driving season and although gasoline stocks are still millions of barrels lower than this time last year the traditional pre-summer bull rally has not materialised," Fenella Graham at MeesPierson Derivatives said in her daily report.

"The problem of looking at gasoline as a guide for the crude market is that the gasoline crack spread has recently been very low and therefore gasoline prices can afford to rally without too much of a pull on the crudes," Graham adds.
American Petroleum Institute (API) data released last week showed U.S. gasoline stocks rose by 800,000 barrels but were still nearly seven million barrels below year ago levels.

This narrow crack margin for products has led to some refiners in Asia and Europe cutting back crude runs. Analysts said this combined with maintenance turnarounds could start to put some pressure on crude prices. The general lack of momentum is also seen keeping crude markets on the defensive for a while.

Taking a more positive point of view, Al Graham at Elliott Wave International, Gainesville, Georgia said, "Going under $21.46 (on crude) postpones for a few days but does not eliminate very bullish longer term expectations."

Of gasoline, he said, "As long as 63.75 cents (on July) support holds, the door is open for more pattern progression to the upside, although crude falling to under $21.46 would increase the chance of a break of this support and a probe of 62.80 cents (a gallon) before the next major upleg begins."

July NYMEX crude added to Friday's losses and last traded 23 cents lower at $21.40 a barrel in ACCESS trade. Unleaded gasoline for June delivery was off over half a cent at around 66.30 cents a gallon with a gap down opening between Friday's 66.92 cent close and opening ACCES trade at 66.55 cents. June heating oil last traded on ACCESS 0.52 cent lower at 57 cents.
